## What it is

Every decision the Maintenance family asks your organization to make before its policy and procedures can be final: the family's key questions, then each organization-defined parameter of every MA control in the baseline, with a typical value where the [Maintenance Policy](/templates/policies/ma/) gives one. Download the spreadsheet, fill the "Your value" column with the people who decide, and carry the values into the policy's highlighted fields.

Typical values are starting points, not recommendations for every system. "Who decides" defaults to the role accountable for the family policy; many organizations delegate system-level values to the system owner.

## Decisions (Moderate baseline)

20 decisions.

| Decision | Control | Typical value | Who decides |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who approves maintenance on each system, and where are the maintenance records kept? | MA-2, MA-2(2) | The system owner approves scheduled maintenance through the change control process and each unscheduled repair before it starts; every activity is recorded in the maintenance log or the IT service management system, and the system owner reviews the records each quarter. | System owner |
| Who may perform nonlocal maintenance, and how do they connect? | MA-4, MA-4(3), MA-5 | Only personnel and maintenance organizations on the authorized list, through the organization's managed remote access service with multi-factor authentication, using a maintenance account that is enabled for each approved session and disabled when it ends; no always-on remote access tools installed by a vendor. | Chief Information Security Officer |
| How are maintenance personnel who lack the required access authorizations handled? | MA-5, MA-5(1) | They work only while escorted and supervised by a technically competent employee who has the required access authorizations, with temporary credentials for that visit or session that are disabled when it ends. | System owner |
| What may leave the facility for repair or replacement, and what must stay? | MA-2, MA-3(3) | Storage media stay; a failed drive is kept and sanitized or destroyed by the organization, under a media retention option in the maintenance contract where available. Other components leave only after sanitization and the system owner's approval. | System owner |
| Which components need contracted maintenance support or spare parts, and how quickly must they be restored? | MA-6 | The components that support essential mission and business functions, and the security components that protect them, with support contracts or spares on hand that restore them within the recovery time objective in the contingency plan. | System owner |
| Personnel or roles to whom the maintenance policy is to be disseminated | MA-1 | Everyone within its scope, through the policy library | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Personnel or roles to whom the maintenance procedures are to be disseminated | MA-1 | The people who carry them out, and the system owners | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Select one or more: organization-level; mission/business process-level; system-level | MA-1 | Organization-level | Chief Information Security Officer |
| An official to manage the maintenance policy and procedures | MA-1 | Chief Information Security Officer | Chief Information Security Officer |
| The frequency with which the current maintenance policy is reviewed and updated | MA-1 | Annually | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Events that would require the current maintenance policy to be reviewed and updated | MA-1 | Assessment or audit findings, security incidents or breaches, and changes in applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards or guidelines | Chief Information Security Officer |
| The frequency with which the current maintenance procedures are reviewed and updated | MA-1 | Annually | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Events that would require the maintenance procedures to be reviewed and updated | MA-1 | The same events as the policy, and changes to the systems, tools or services the procedures describe | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Personnel or roles required to explicitly approve the removal of the system or system components from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance or repairs | MA-2 | The system owner | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Information to be removed from associated media prior to removal from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance, repair, or replacement | MA-2 | All organizational information, including personally identifiable information, credentials and cryptographic keys | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Information to be included in organizational maintenance records | MA-2 | The date and time, the system and component, a description of the maintenance performed, the names and organization of the individuals performing it, the escort's name, the components or equipment removed or replaced, the approval, and the result of the post-maintenance control check | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Frequency at which to review previously approved system maintenance tools | MA-3 | At least annually | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Personnel or roles who can authorize removal of equipment from the facility | MA-3(3) | The Chief Information Security Officer | Chief Information Security Officer |
| System components for which maintenance support and/or spare parts are obtained | MA-6 | The components that support essential mission and business functions, as the business impact analysis identifies them, and the security components that protect them | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Time period within which maintenance support and/or spare parts are to be obtained after a failure | MA-6 | The recovery time objective set in the contingency plan from the business impact analysis | Chief Information Security Officer |
